CONSTRUCTION SKILLS
12.1 INTRODUCTION
The artof stitching is acombination ofmany skills.Manyprocesses are used in constructing
a garment and giving it its final.form. The same process cannot be used in making all
garments - different processes are used for different garments, such as facing, binding,
zips, etc. If one does not have adequate knowledge of all these processes one will not
be able to make garments of various types and designs. Hence, one needs to have
knowledge of the various processes involved like collars, designing, etc. Let us find out
more about these in this lesson.

12.3 FACING
The cloth used to bind the raw edges of upper garments by folding inwards, is called
facing.
12.4
TYPES OF FACING
Necklines are generally finished with a facing. Facings are suitable forthick fabrics. They
are generally done by two methods, which are as follows -
1.
A bias strip can be used for the facing but this is generally done when a narrow
facing is to be done. The bias trip is cut W' wide and is stitched along the edge
of the neckline or the armhole. While stitching, care should be taken not to stretch
the bias strip. This gives a good finishing without pulling the neckline out of shape.
After stitching along the edge, the bias strip is turned inside towards the wrong
side ofthe garment. It is then folded in and hemmed into place.
2.
For a wider facing, a strip cut in the shape ofthe neckline is used. The right side
of the garment is placed over a piece of cloth and a running stitch is made along
the neckline. After this, the neckline is stitched into place. After stitching, the cloth
is cut along the neckline. The cloth is also cut in the same shape on the other side
leaving a margin of 1W' to 2". This strip is then turned over and is either hemmed
or stitched to give a neat edge. Sometimes a very wide strip maybe used and in
that case, the shaped strip is simply turned in and stitched along the edge from the
front so that it does not show. In this way a facing can be used to finish the raw
edge of necklines, etc.

BINDING
The rolled edge formed after attaching a bias strip to a raw edge is called a binding. The

The piping made by attaching bias strips is known as bias piping. To make this,
.a square piece of cloth is folded at an angle of 45° and cut into strips. The bias
strip is stretched while attaching and then folded to give a thin rolled edge and
hemmed into place. The thinner the rolled edge, the better the piping looks.

12.8 ELASTIC
Elastic are of various kinds like - round, flat, narrow, wide, etc. They are used in different
garments. The method of using elastic is different in different garments such as in pyjama
bottoms, in pyjama belt or in skirts and knickers.
In pyjama belt, the elastic used is 2 points wide. It is inserted with the help of a safety pin.
The two edges are drawn up and placed on top of each other and stitched securely. Care
must be taken to see that the elastic does not twist while threading otherwise it will hurt
the wearer.
A broader elastic is used in knickers. The cloth left for the belt is turned to the right side.
The elastic is placed on top and is stitched first at the top and then the bottom edge. The
cloth is then turned over and stitched in place. Parallel rows of stitching is then made on
the elastic belt which serve two purposes - one, the elastic does fiot twist at any point and
two, the slight pleats which appear look attractive.
When attaching elastic on the bottom of sleeves or pyjamas, the elastic is placed about
1"inside the edge and stretched and stitched into place. This results in small pleats which
make a small frill at the edge. Round elastic can also be used in pyjamas.
In this way, elastics are used different garments.

12.9
DESIGN DART
Darts are used to either give fullness or close fitting according to the figure of the person.
Darts can be made in different ways - by cutting the cloth and then stitching it or by
diagonally stitching the excess cloth at the place fullness is desired.
Dart
The diagonal line of stitching given 'on a fold of cloth which is broad at one end and
tapering to one or both ends, is known as dart. Darts give fullness to the heavier parts of
the body. Darts are mainly of two types-

Construction Skills :: 115
i)
Single point dart
The single point dart is used in skirts, blouses, vests, etc. It is broad at one end
and pointed at the other.
ii)
Double point dart
The double point dart is pointed at both ends. It is generally used in ladies suit.
Darts are placed at different places in different garments. They derive their name
according to their placements, such as-
~
Waist dart
it)
Side dart
ill)
Armhole dart
iv)
Center front dart
v)
Shoulder dart
vi)

vii)

viii)

Rules for making darts
In order to make neat darts, the following rules must be followed.
1.
While making darts, the beginning and the end of the seam should be made doubly
secure.
2.
If the dart is very wide at one end, flatten the dart from the center while attaching
to another piece.
3.
The width of a double point dart at the center should be 1 to 1Y2 ems.
4.
In thick fabrics, the dart is cut from the center and the cloth spread on both sides
or pressed open.
There are some other darts used in dress making which are conventionally not called
darts, such as french dart, panel dart, fish dart, etc.
French dart
The french dart is made in ladies kurta from the bust point to small hip. [Fig 12.5 (a)]
Fist dart
This dart is used while joining the bodice to the sleeve. It is shaped like a fish hence it is
called a fish dart. [Fig 12.5 (b)]

Panel dart
To make this dart, the entire length of cloth which would be folded inside the dart, is cut
away and the two edges stitched together to give fitting to the garment, It is used in smart
fitting petticoats. It is also used in jackets, coats, etc. The'dart is not visible either from.
the right or from the wrong side of the garment as the dart is made by removing the cloth
ofthe dart and joining the two sides. In this way, different darts are made.

12.10 YOKE AND MID RIFT
YOKE
The piece of cloth attached to the upper part of a garment is called a yoke. It may be of
the same cloth as the garment or it may be different.

Construction Skills :: 117
Need for yoke
1.
To increase the strength of the garment.
2.
To change the direction of the cloth to prevent stretching.
3.
To make a fashionable design.:
4.
To balance the weight ofthe dress.
Yoke is generallyused in the upper body garments. Sometimes may also beused in lower
body garments. Yoke are used in the following places-
1.
Shoulders of shirts
2.
Front and back ofladies garments.
3.
Below the belt in skirts - front and back.
4.
Waist line of maxi.
5.
Back orhip ofheavy garments likejeans. It is difficult to make darts injeans hence
ayoke is used for fitting.
6.
One piece front and back yoke for design.
Yoke are sometimes made of double layer cloth but is made of single layer only in thick
fabrics. The place where a yoke is attached should be made secure with double row .
stitching.
Yoke may sometimes be used to increase the length ofthe garment or may be maae in
a contrasting cloth to create interesting designs.
#,<:
Yoke is generally cut on the cross grain and is often used at the back of men's shirt and
injeans. The width of the yoke varies with fashion. When we need a flaired skirt but a
fitted waist, we make use of a yoke. In this way a yoke can be used variously in different
garments.

MIDRIFT
The design or pleat used in the middle/center of any garment is known as midrift. The cloth
pleated at the back, under the yoke, in men's shirts, is a midrift. In effect, it is a device
used to adjust the cloth ofthe back of a shirt to the yoke piece. Since loose fitting shirts
are preferred these days, a pleat is made at the back. This adds to the beauty of the shirt
as well. The midrift is also used as a design in ladies suit. Two types of pleats are used
to make a midrift. They are -

12.11 BELT
•
A belt is used to make a fitted waist. It is used in pants, knickers,
skirts, etc. Belts.are
of two types and are used in two ways. These-are-

1.
Frock belt
A frock is generally made quite loose for children and a belt is used to tighten it
slightly at the waist. It is attached to the yoke which is generally a plain yoke. A
belt is similarly used in house coats but the belt used is straight and.is not fixed.
The belt of a frock is cut on a bias. It is stitched along two edges by keeping right
sides.facing and then turned inside out. It is properly pressed and is then attached
to the sides ofthe bodice.

In this collar halfthe collar stands up-and the other halfturns and rolls over. The stand and
the fall can be made separately too. Aonepiece
collaris made as an open collar. This
type of collar is made in shirts, bushirts, shirts of safari suits etc.
In garments like gowns, the collar is cut as a part ofthe front piece. The lapel is made
by keeping extra cloth beyond the center front line. The lining which is used in such a collar
is of the same cloth as the garment. In garments like coat and gown, the line at which the
collar folds and falls back on the garment is known as the lapel break line; The lapel is
folded and stitched. A tape or braid can be used on the fold to prevent spreading or
flattening.
